text_en: Among the chairs going home, one has a strip of red cloth tied beneath the seat. Jori checks the knot before lifting it.
This one belongs to the house with the low door.
I remember the owner. She brought the sharp little onions.
You remember everybody by the sound or the food.
Very reliable methods of finding people at supper.
The repaired chair stays in the square, where the innkeeper said it could stay.
Take the other side. The door is lower than the chair is wide.
I could make a verse of the return journey.
It is twelve steps.
A short verse.
Keep your hand under the seat. That will be more useful.
Pippa adjusts her grip. They reach the door without an audience following them.
Useful can be quiet. I am practicing.
There it is. I thought you might decide it belonged to the square now.
It belonged to the square for supper. It belongs here again.
It had a very good evening.
It is a chair. I had the evening.
Jori turns the seat to pass the threshold without scraping it.
The brace held. Thank you for lending something you use.
I sit here when I peel onions. Tonight somebody else got the seat.
Then we brought it back before the next bowl of onions.
A considerate timetable.
I saw you laugh before the last verse. Jori was defending the soup from criticism.
I was criticizing the soup.
Yes. That was the part I liked.
Then that is a very good part to keep.
The chair returns to the patch of floor beside the low window. The owner rests one hand on its back.
The square sounded different with everybody sitting close.
Will you lend it again?
Ask when there is another supper. I might bring onions again.
We will remember the door.
The red cloth stays tied beneath the seat. It catches the light from the low window.
She kept a different part of the evening than I did.
She was sitting somewhere else.
That is annoyingly sensible.
Keep your hands free. There are bowls to bring inside.
They return to the square while the last dishes are being stacked. The chair is already home.
